**[Section 11: Seller\'s Credit Support]{.underline}**

**11.1 Performance Bond.** Seller shall provide a performance bond in the amount of seven million five hundred thousand dollars (\$7,500,000) issued by a creditworthy surety company rated at least A-- by Atlas Credit Services (or equivalent rating from a nationally recognized rating agency).

**11.2 Timing.** The performance bond shall be posted no later than thirty (30) days prior to the commencement of Project construction.

**11.3 Term and Step-Down.** The performance bond shall remain in full force and effect for the first five (5) Contract Years following COD, after which the bond amount shall be reduced to three million seven hundred fifty thousand dollars (\$3,750,000) for the remainder of the Term, or in accordance with such other step-down schedule as the Parties may agree upon in the Definitive PPA.

**11.4 Surety. Seller anticipates that the performance bond will be issued by Highpoint Surety & Hartleigh Co. or another surety meeting the rating requirement specified in Section 11.1.**

**[Section 12: Buyer\'s Credit Support]{.underline}**

**12.1 No Credit Support Required.** No credit support shall be required from Buyer in connection with the Definitive PPA or its obligations thereunder.

**12.2 Rationale.** Buyer is an investment-grade municipal entity holding credit ratings of A2 from Sterling Ratings Agency and A from Atlas Credit Services. Buyer represents that it has the legal authority and financial capacity to perform its obligations under the Definitive PPA throughout the Term.

**[Section 13: Change of Law]{.underline}**

**13.1 General Rule.** Each Party shall bear its own increased costs resulting from any change in applicable law, regulation, rule, ordinance, or governmental order occurring after the date of execution of the Definitive PPA (a \"Change of Law\"), except as specifically provided in Section 13.2 below.

**13.2 Exception --- New Transmission Charges.** Notwithstanding Section 13.1, Buyer shall bear one hundred percent (100%) of any new transmission charges, transmission access fees, ancillary service charges, or other transmission-related costs imposed on the Project or on the delivery of energy from the Project to the Delivery Point by any governmental authority, transmission provider, regional transmission organization (including the Southwest Power Pool), independent system operator, or balancing authority after the date of execution of the Definitive PPA. This allocation reflects the Parties\' agreement that Buyer, as the direct beneficiary of the delivered energy and as a municipal utility with the ability to manage transmission cost exposure through its member municipality rate structures, is in the best position to bear the risk of new or increased transmission-related charges that may be imposed following execution of the Definitive PPA.

**[Section 14: Force Majeure]{.underline}**

**14.1 Definition.** \"Force Majeure\" means any event or circumstance beyond the reasonable control of the affected Party that could not have been avoided or overcome by the exercise of reasonable diligence, including but not limited to: acts of God; earthquakes, floods, hurricanes, tornadoes, ice storms, or other natural disasters; wars (whether declared or undeclared), armed conflicts, or military actions; acts of terrorism or sabotage; epidemics, pandemics, or public health emergencies; governmental actions, including changes in law, embargoes, or sanctions; grid emergencies or blackouts ordered by the regional transmission organization or balancing authority; fire, explosion, or equipment failure not attributable to the negligence of the affected Party; and labor strikes or lockouts affecting the Project or critical suppliers. Force Majeure shall not include (i) changes in market conditions, commodity prices, or economic conditions, (ii) the inability to obtain financing, (iii) equipment or material delivery delays that could have been reasonably anticipated, or (iv) weather conditions within the normal range for the Project site.

**14.2 Notice and Mitigation.** The affected Party shall provide prompt written notice to the other Party of any Force Majeure event, describing the event, its expected duration, and the obligations affected. The affected Party shall use commercially reasonable efforts to mitigate the effects of the Force Majeure event and to resume performance as promptly as practicable.

**14.3 Suspension of Obligations.** Neither Party shall be liable for any failure or delay in performance to the extent caused by a Force Majeure event, and the affected Party\'s obligations shall be suspended to the extent and for the duration that performance is prevented by the Force Majeure event. The Term of the Definitive PPA shall not be extended by reason of any Force Majeure event.

**14.4 Termination Right.** If a Force Majeure event continues for a continuous period of eighteen (18) months and prevents a material portion of either Party\'s performance under the Definitive PPA, either Party may terminate the Definitive PPA without liability to the other Party by providing thirty (30) days\' prior written notice to the other Party, such notice to be delivered no earlier than the expiration of the eighteen (18) month period. Upon such termination, neither Party shall have any further obligation to the other Party, except for obligations accrued prior to the date of termination.

**[Section 15: Assignment]{.underline}**

**15.1 Collateral Assignment to Financing Parties.** Seller may collaterally assign its rights and interests under the Definitive PPA to Financing Parties (including senior secured lenders and tax equity investors) without the prior consent of Buyer. Buyer shall, at Seller\'s request and at no cost to Buyer, execute and deliver a commercially reasonable consent and agreement to any such Financing Party (including any tax equity investor), acknowledging such collateral assignment and providing customary step-in rights, cure rights, and other lender or investor protections reasonably requested by such Financing Party. Buyer\'s obligation to deliver such consent and agreement shall be a material covenant of the Definitive PPA.

**15.2 Full Assignment.** Any full or outright assignment by either Party of its rights or obligations under the Definitive PPA (other than a collateral assignment by Seller described in Section 15.1) shall require the prior written consent of the other Party, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed.

**15.3 Change of Control.** A change of control of Seller (whether by merger, consolidation, sale of equity interests, or otherwise) shall not be deemed an assignment requiring Buyer\'s consent under Section 15.2, provided that Seller gives Buyer not less than thirty (30) days\' prior written notice of any such change of control and the surviving or acquiring entity assumes in writing all of Seller\'s obligations under the Definitive PPA.

**[Section 16: Governing Law]{.underline}**

The Definitive PPA shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Oklahoma, without regard to its conflict-of-laws principles.

**[Section 17: Dispute Resolution]{.underline}**

**17.1 Step 1 --- Mediation.** Any dispute, controversy, or claim arising out of or relating to the Definitive PPA, or the breach, termination, or invalidity thereof, shall first be submitted to non-binding mediation, to be conducted in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma, in accordance with the mediation rules of the American Arbitration Association (\"AAA\"). Each Party shall designate a senior representative with authority to settle the dispute to participate in the mediation. The Parties shall endeavor to select a mutually acceptable mediator within fifteen (15) days of the date on which either Party delivers a written request for mediation to the other Party.

**17.2 Step 2 --- Binding Arbitration.** If the dispute is not resolved through mediation within sixty (60) days of the commencement of mediation proceedings (or such longer period as the Parties may agree in writing), either Party may submit the dispute to binding arbitration under the AAA Commercial Arbitration Rules. The arbitration shall be conducted by a panel of three (3) arbitrators, selected in accordance with the AAA\'s arbitrator selection procedures, and shall be seated in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma. The arbitration proceedings shall be conducted in the English language. The arbitrators shall render a written, reasoned award within sixty (60) days of the close of the arbitration hearing, or such longer period as the arbitrators may deem necessary.

**17.3 Finality.** The arbitrators\' award shall be final and binding upon the Parties and may be entered as a judgment in any court of competent jurisdiction in the State of Oklahoma or elsewhere.

**17.4 Confidentiality.** The arbitration and all related proceedings shall be confidential. Neither Party shall disclose the existence, content, or results of any mediation or arbitration proceeding, including the arbitrators\' award, except (a) as required by applicable law, regulation, or order of a court or governmental authority, (b) to a Party\'s legal counsel, auditors, or Financing Parties on a confidential basis, or (c) with the prior written consent of the other Party.

**17.5 Costs.** Each Party shall bear its own attorneys\' fees and costs in connection with any mediation or arbitration proceeding. The Parties shall share equally the fees of the mediator, the arbitrators, and the AAA.

**[Section 18: Binding Nature and Conditions Precedent]{.underline}**

**18.1 Binding Effect.** This Term Sheet is binding on both Parties and constitutes a legally enforceable agreement with respect to the commercial terms set forth herein. Each Party represents and warrants that it has full authority to enter into this Term Sheet and to perform its obligations hereunder, and that the execution and delivery of this Term Sheet has been duly authorized by all necessary corporate or governmental action.

**18.2 Negotiation of Definitive PPA.** The Parties shall negotiate in good faith and use commercially reasonable efforts to execute a Definitive PPA within ninety (90) days of the date of this Term Sheet (i.e., by February 6, 2025), which deadline may be extended by mutual written consent of the Parties. The Definitive PPA shall incorporate and be consistent with the commercial terms set forth in this Term Sheet.

**18.3 Conditions Precedent.** Execution of the Definitive PPA shall be subject to the satisfaction (or written waiver) of each of the following conditions precedent:

> \(a\) completion of customary due diligence by each Party, including technical, environmental, legal, and financial due diligence with respect to the Project and the counterparty;
>
> \(b\) approval of the Definitive PPA by the Board of Directors (or equivalent governing body) of each Party, including, in the case of Buyer, approval by the Lakeshore Municipal Electric Authority Board of Trustees;
>
> \(c\) no material adverse change in the creditworthiness, financial condition, or operational capacity of either Party between the date of this Term Sheet and the date of execution of the Definitive PPA; and
>
> \(d\) receipt by Seller of all material permits, approvals, licenses, and authorizations necessary to commence construction of the Project, or reasonable assurance (as determined by Seller in its commercially reasonable judgment) that such permits and approvals will be obtained in a timely manner.

**18.4 Termination of Term Sheet.** If the Definitive PPA is not executed within the ninety (90) day period specified in Section 18.2 (as may be extended by mutual written consent), either Party may terminate this Term Sheet upon thirty (30) days\' prior written notice to the other Party; provided, however, that the terminating Party is not then in breach of its obligation to negotiate in good faith as set forth in Section 18.2.

**18.5 Relationship to Definitive PPA.** In the event of any conflict between the terms of this Term Sheet and the terms of the Definitive PPA, the terms of the Definitive PPA shall control; provided, however, that this Term Sheet shall remain relevant for purposes of interpreting the Parties\' intent with respect to any ambiguity in the Definitive PPA.

**18.6 Amendments.** Any amendment, modification, or waiver of any provision of this Term Sheet shall be effective only if made in writing and signed by both Parties. No oral agreement, course of dealing, or course of performance shall be sufficient to amend or modify the terms of this Term Sheet.

 translation as we finalize the PPA:

**Curtailment Compensation Rate.** The curtailment compensation rate should r=
emain at 90% of the contract price, consistent with the term sheet. We did no=
t agree to any reduction. I recall Jeffrey floated reducing it to 80% in his =
first markup, but we pushed back and I believe Tamara confirmed they would ho=
ld at 90%. Please make sure the final PPA reflects 90%.

**Escalation Rate.** The 1.5% annual escalation starting Year 6 was not discu=
ssed as a point of negotiation =E2=80=94 both sides accepted the term sheet p=
ricing formula. Please just confirm the pricing table in Exhibit B ties out t=
o the 1.5% compound escalation. I don't want any rounding issues creating dis=
crepancies.

**Delay Liquidated Damages.** The delay LDs of $125,000/month capped at $1.5 =
million over 12 months should carry over from the term sheet as-is. We didn't=
 negotiate any changes here.

**Force Majeure Termination Period.** The 18-month FM cure period before eith=
er party can terminate was important to us and we did not agree to shorten it=
. This should remain at 18 months.

**Change of Law / New Transmission Charges.** The term sheet is clear that Bu=
yer bears 100% of any new transmission charges imposed after execution. I kno=
w Jeffrey's initial draft had a generic "each party bears its own costs" chan=
ge-of-law clause. We pushed back on that in our first set of comments. Please=
 make sure the final draft includes the specific carve-out for new transmissi=
on charges as Buyer's responsibility.

**Mechanical Availability LD Rate.** The $50,000/percentage point mechanical =
availability LD rate from the term sheet should carry forward unchanged.

**Dispute Resolution.** We specifically want arbitration per the term sheet =
=E2=80=94 mediation followed by binding arbitration under AAA Commercial Rule=
s, seated in Oklahoma City. Jeffrey's first draft had litigation in Osage Cou=
nty district court. We flagged that as unacceptable and I believe he agreed t=
o revert to arbitration. Please confirm this is reflected in whatever comes b=
ack.

---

**3. Financing Party Definition and Tax Equity Assignment**

This is probably the most important structural point for Ridgeline's diligenc=
e. The term sheet allows us to collaterally assign to lenders AND tax equity =
investors without Buyer consent. I raised this specifically with Jeffrey Lang=
don on our January 17 call, and he confirmed that Prescott & Hale would defin=
e "Financing Parties" broadly enough to include tax equity investors in a par=
tnership-flip structure =E2=80=94 not just senior secured lenders.

As you know, Priya Venkataraman at Ridgeline has emphasized =E2=80=94 includi=
ng in the January 10 tax equity commitment letter =E2=80=94 that the partners=
hip-flip structure requires Ridgeline to have consent-free collateral assignm=
ent rights and step-in rights under the PPA. This is not negotiable from thei=
r side. Jeffrey said he understood the issue and would make sure the definiti=
on covers it. Please double-check this in whatever draft comes back. If the "=
Financing Party" definition is limited to senior secured debt providers, we h=
ave a problem =E2=80=94 Ridgeline won't close.

I'll note that Ridgeline's due diligence checklist (the one Priya circulated)=
 specifically asks about this point, and any deficiency will be flagged immed=
iately. We cannot afford to be going back to Lakeshore on this after executio=
n.

---

**4. Items Still Being Discussed**

A couple of points remain in active discussion:

**REC Ownership for Excess Generation.** Tamara raised the idea of us keeping=
 RECs on any generation above 100% of contract quantity in a given year. The =
term sheet says all RECs transfer to Buyer bundled with the energy, so this w=
ould be a deviation. I'm inclined to accept this if they offer it =E2=80=94 t=
here's real value in retaining excess RECs for separate sale =E2=80=94 but I =
want to flag it as a change from the term sheet. If we agree to it, let's mak=
e sure it's cleanly drafted so there's no ambiguity about the boundary betwee=
n bundled and unbundled RECs.

**Early COD Provision.** Lakeshore is fine with us achieving COD as early as =
March 1, 2026, rather than the 3 months before Guaranteed COD in the term she=
et. This just gives us more scheduling flexibility and is a straightforward i=
mprovement. I don't see any downside.

---

**5. Timeline and Next Steps**

Prescott & Hale is expected to circulate a near-final PPA draft by January 27=
 or 28. Catherine, I'd like to ask you and Ryan to turn comments within 3=E2=
=80=934 business days so we can target execution by early-to-mid February.

As a reminder on the financing timeline: Ridgeline's deviation report is due =
March 14, and our target financial close with both Ridgeline Capital Partners=
 ($116.25 million tax equity) and Elkhorn Infrastructure Credit ($232.5 milli=
on construction loan) is April 15. Any unexplained deviations from the term s=
heet are going to create diligence issues with Ridgeline and potentially Elkh=
orn, so it's critical that we get the PPA right before we sign it. I'd rather=
 take an extra few days on the front end than deal with post-execution cleanu=
p.

If there's anything I've missed or if you see concerns I'm not flagging, plea=
se call me.

---

Thank you both for your work on this =E2=80=94 I know it's been a grind. I'll=
 be in Oklahoma City on Monday the 27th and happy to stop by Meridian Tower t=
o discuss any of this in person if that would be helpful.

Best,
Dana

**[POWER PURCHASE AGREEMENT]{.underline}**

**Prairie Crest Wind Project**

**250 MW Wind Energy Facility** **Osage County, Oklahoma**

by and between

**LAKESHORE MUNICIPAL ELECTRIC AUTHORITY** as Buyer

and

**CRESCENT RIDGE WIND PARTNERS LLC** as Seller

Dated as of February 4, 2025

*Prepared by Prescott & Hale LLP, Counsel to Buyer*

**[POWER PURCHASE AGREEMENT]{.underline}**

This POWER PURCHASE AGREEMENT (this \"Agreement\") is entered into as of February 4, 2025 (the \"Effective Date\"), by and between:

**CRESCENT RIDGE WIND PARTNERS LLC**, a Delaware limited liability company (\"Seller\"), formed on February 12, 2023, with its principal business office at 4400 Meridian Tower, Suite 1500, Oklahoma City, OK 73102, and its registered office at 1301 Market Street, Wilmington, DE 19801; and

**LAKESHORE MUNICIPAL ELECTRIC AUTHORITY**, a municipal electric utility organized and existing under Title 11, Chapter 30 of the Oklahoma Municipal Power Act (\"Buyer\"), with its principal office at 723 South Main Street, Stillwater, OK 74074.

Seller and Buyer are sometimes referred to herein individually as a \"Party\" and collectively as the \"Parties.\"

**RECITALS**

WHEREAS, Seller is a wholly owned subsidiary of Verdana Renewable Holdings Inc., a Delaware corporation, and is developing a 250 MW nameplate capacity wind-powered electric generating facility known as the \"Prairie Crest Wind Project\" (the \"Facility\") located on approximately 14,200 leased acres in Osage County, Oklahoma, consisting of sixty-two (62) Nordex Delta4000 4.0 MW wind turbine generators plus two (2) reserve turbine pads, with interconnection to the Southwest Power Pool (\"SPP\") transmission system at SPP interconnection queue position GEN-2205;

WHEREAS, Buyer is a municipal electric utility that serves approximately sixty-eight thousand (68,000) retail electric customers across its four (4) member municipalities, namely the cities of Stillwater, Ponca City, Blackwell, and Perry, Oklahoma, and has a current peak demand of approximately 480 MW;

WHEREAS, Buyer has adopted a renewable portfolio target of thirty percent (30%) of its total energy supply from renewable energy resources by the year 2030, and currently derives approximately eleven percent (11%) of its energy supply from qualifying renewable energy resources, and Buyer desires to procure additional renewable energy and associated environmental attributes to advance toward such target;

WHEREAS, the Parties executed that certain Binding Term Sheet dated November 8, 2024 (the \"Term Sheet\"), setting forth the principal terms under which Seller would sell and Buyer would purchase the energy output and associated environmental attributes of the Facility, and the Parties now desire to enter into this definitive Power Purchase Agreement on the terms and conditions set forth herein, which supersedes the Term Sheet to the extent inconsistent;

WHEREAS, Buyer holds investment-grade credit ratings of A2 by Sterling Ratings Agency and A by Atlas Credit Services, each as of the Effective Date, and Seller has relied upon such credit ratings in entering into this Agreement;

WHEREAS, Seller has obtained SPP interconnection queue position GEN-2205 and is proceeding with the interconnection study process in accordance with SPP\'s Open Access Transmission Tariff and applicable SPP business practices; and

WHEREAS, the Parties desire to set forth their respective rights and obligations with respect to the development, construction, operation, and maintenance of the Facility, the sale and purchase of the Net Energy Output of the Facility, and the transfer of Environmental Attributes associated therewith, all on the terms and subject to the conditions set forth herein.

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements hereinafter set forth, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:

**[ARTICLE 1 --- DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATION]{.underline}**

**Section 1.1 --- Definitions**

Capitalized terms used in this Agreement shall have the meanings set forth in Exhibit A hereto, unless otherwise defined in the body of this Agreement. Any capitalized term used in this Agreement and not defined herein or in Exhibit A shall have the meaning ascribed to such term by the SPP Open Access Transmission Tariff, as applicable.

**Section 1.2 --- Rules of Interpretation**

The following rules of interpretation shall apply to this Agreement:

\(a\) References in this Agreement to any Article, Section, clause, Exhibit, or Schedule shall, unless otherwise specified, be references to an Article, Section, clause, Exhibit, or Schedule of or to this Agreement.

\(b\) The headings and subheadings contained in this Agreement are inserted for convenience of reference only and shall not affect the meaning or interpretation of this Agreement or any provision hereof.

\(c\) The word \"including\" and variations thereof (such as \"include\" and \"includes\") shall mean \"including without limitation.\"

\(d\) Unless the context otherwise requires, words importing the singular include the plural and vice versa, and words importing a gender include all genders.

\(e\) References to any Person include such Person\'s permitted successors and assigns.

\(f\) References to any Applicable Law shall mean such Applicable Law as amended, modified, supplemented, or replaced from time to time, and all rules and regulations promulgated thereunder, unless the context requires otherwise.

\(g\) Unless otherwise specified, all references to days shall mean calendar days. If any period expires on a day that is not a Business Day, such period shall be extended to the next succeeding Business Day.

\(h\) All references to times of day shall be to Central Prevailing Time, meaning Central Standard Time or Central Daylight Time, as applicable.

\(i\) All monetary amounts stated in this Agreement are in United States dollars unless otherwise specified.

\(j\) The words \"hereof,\" \"herein,\" \"hereunder,\" and similar terms refer to this Agreement as a whole and not to any particular provision of this Agreement.

\(k\) The Parties have participated jointly in the negotiation and drafting of this Agreement. In the event an ambiguity or question of intent arises, this Agreement shall be construed as if drafted jointly by the Parties, and no presumption or burden of proof shall arise favoring or disfavoring any Party by virtue of the authorship of any provision of this Agreement.

**Section 1.3 --- Order of Precedence**

In the event of a conflict or inconsistency between the body of this Agreement (Articles 1 through 20) and any Exhibit attached hereto, the body of this Agreement shall control and take precedence over such Exhibit. In the event of a conflict or inconsistency among the Exhibits, the order of precedence shall be as follows, with the first-listed Exhibit taking highest priority: (i) Exhibit A (Definitions), (ii) Exhibit B (Pricing Schedule and Price Table), (iii) Exhibit C (Project Description), (iv) Exhibit D (Metering), (v) Exhibit E (Insurance Requirements), (vi) Exhibit F (Form of Performance Bond), (vii) Exhibit G (Guaranteed Dates and Milestones), and (viii) Exhibit H (Form of Lender Consent). The Parties shall use commercially reasonable efforts to resolve any ambiguity in a manner that gives effect to the original intent of the Parties as reflected in the body of this Agreement.

**[ARTICLE 2 --- TERM AND CONDITIONS PRECEDENT]{.underline}**

**Section 2.1 --- Effective Date**

This Agreement shall become effective as of the date first written above (the \"Effective Date\"), which is February 4, 2025. Each Party represents and warrants that the individual executing this Agreement on its behalf has been duly authorized to do so.

**Section 2.2 --- Term**

The term of this Agreement (the \"Term\") shall commence on the Effective Date and shall continue for a period of twenty (20) Contract Years following the Commercial Operation Date, unless earlier terminated in accordance with the provisions hereof. For purposes of this Agreement, \"Contract Year\" means each successive twelve (12) month period commencing on the Commercial Operation Date (or each anniversary thereof). The first Contract Year shall commence on the Commercial Operation Date and end on the day immediately preceding the first anniversary of the Commercial Operation Date. Each subsequent Contract Year shall commence on the applicable anniversary of the Commercial Operation Date.

**Section 2.3 --- Conditions Precedent to Seller\'s Obligations**

The obligations of Seller to sell and deliver Net Energy Output under this Agreement shall be subject to the satisfaction or waiver (to the extent permitted by Applicable Law) of each of the following conditions precedent:

\(a\) Seller shall have received all material governmental approvals, permits, licenses, and authorizations required for the construction, ownership, and operation of the Facility, including all environmental permits, land use approvals, and Federal Aviation Administration determinations of no hazard, in each case in form and substance satisfactory to Seller in its reasonable discretion;

\(b\) Seller shall have executed and delivered, and the SPP shall have accepted, a definitive Large Generator Interconnection Agreement for the Facility at SPP interconnection queue position GEN-2205, which agreement shall be in full force and effect;

\(c\) Seller shall have completed construction and commissioning of the Facility in accordance with the requirements of Section 3.2 and shall have achieved the Commercial Operation Date;

\(d\) Buyer shall have delivered to Seller such credit support, if any, as may be required pursuant to Section 13.2 and Section 13.3; and

\(e\) No Material Adverse Change shall have occurred with respect to Buyer\'s creditworthiness, as determined in good faith by Seller. For purposes of this Section 2.3(e), \"Material Adverse Change\" means a downgrade of Buyer\'s credit rating below investment grade (i.e., below Baa3 by Sterling Ratings Agency or below BBB-- by Atlas Credit Services).

**Section 2.4 --- Conditions Precedent to Buyer\'s Obligations**

The obligations of Buyer to purchase and receive Net Energy Output under this Agreement shall be subject to the satisfaction or waiver (to the extent permitted by Applicable Law) of each of the following conditions precedent:

\(a\) Seller shall have delivered to Buyer the Performance Bond required by Section 13.1, in form and substance as set forth in Exhibit F, issued by a surety company rated at least A-- by Atlas Credit Services;

\(b\) Seller shall have achieved the Commercial Operation Date on or before the Guaranteed Commercial Operation Date, or, if the Guaranteed Commercial Operation Date has not been achieved, Delay LDs shall have commenced accruing and the Outside Date shall not have occurred;

\(c\) Seller shall have delivered to Buyer evidence of all insurance coverages required by Article 15 and Exhibit E, in form and substance reasonably satisfactory to Buyer; and

\(d\) Each of Seller\'s representations and warranties set forth in Section 11.1 shall be true and correct in all material respects as of the Effective Date and as of the Commercial Operation Date (except to the extent such representations and warranties relate to an earlier date, in which case they shall be true and correct as of such earlier date).

**[ARTICLE 3 --- FACILITY DEVELOPMENT AND COMMERCIAL OPERATION]{.underline}**

**Section 3.1 --- Construction Obligations**

Seller shall design, engineer, procure, construct, and commission the Facility in accordance with Prudent Utility Practice, all Applicable Laws, all applicable governmental permits and authorizations, and the project description set forth in Exhibit C. Seller shall use commercially reasonable efforts to achieve the Commercial Operation Date by the Expected COD of June 1, 2026. Throughout the construction period, Seller shall be solely responsible for all costs associated with the design, engineering, procurement, construction, testing, and commissioning of the Facility, including the cost of obtaining and maintaining all permits and approvals, the cost of all equipment and materials, and all labor costs. Seller shall construct the Facility using new equipment and materials that are suitable for their intended purpose and that conform to the specifications set forth in Exhibit C.

Seller shall be solely responsible for the selection of all contractors and subcontractors engaged in connection with the construction of the Facility, provided that Seller shall require all such contractors and subcontractors to comply with all Applicable Laws and to maintain insurance coverages consistent with industry standards. Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed to make Buyer responsible for, or a party to, any contract between Seller and any of its contractors or subcontractors.

**Section 3.2 --- Guaranteed Commercial Operation Date**

The \"Guaranteed Commercial Operation Date\" shall be September 1, 2026. The Commercial Operation Date (\"COD\") shall be deemed to have occurred on the date upon which all of the following conditions have been satisfied:

\(i\) The Facility shall be capable of generating at least two hundred forty megawatts (240 MW) of electric energy, representing ninety-six percent (96%) of the Facility\'s 250 MW nameplate capacity, as demonstrated by a capacity test conducted in accordance with the testing protocols set forth in Exhibit C, Section 4;

\(ii\) The Large Generator Interconnection Agreement with SPP for interconnection queue position GEN-2205 shall be in full force and effect, and the Facility shall be physically interconnected to the SPP transmission system at the Delivery Point;

\(iii\) Seller shall have obtained all permits, licenses, and governmental approvals required for the commercial operation of the Facility under all Applicable Laws, and all such permits, licenses, and approvals shall be in full force and effect;

\(iv\) The metering equipment at the Delivery Point shall have been installed, tested, and certified in accordance with Exhibit D, and such metering equipment shall be operational and communicating meter data in accordance with Section 7.1;

\(v\) Seller shall have delivered to Buyer a written notice (the \"COD Notice\") certifying that all of the foregoing conditions have been satisfied, accompanied by supporting documentation in form and substance reasonably satisfactory to Buyer, including the results of the capacity test referenced in clause (i) above; and

\(vi\) Buyer shall have had a period of not less than ten (10) Business Days following receipt of the COD Notice to review the supporting documentation and either confirm or reasonably object to Seller\'s certification of COD.

**Section 3.3 --- Early Commercial Operation**

Seller may declare the Commercial Operation Date as early as March 1, 2026, upon not less than sixty (60) days\' prior written notice to Buyer, provided that all conditions set forth in Section 3.2 have been satisfied as of the date specified in such notice. If Seller achieves COD prior to June 1, 2026, the first Contract Year shall nevertheless commence on the actual COD, and the Term shall be measured from such earlier date. Buyer shall cooperate in good faith with Seller to accommodate any scheduling or administrative adjustments necessary to accommodate early Commercial Operation.

**Section 3.4 --- Progress Reporting**

During the period commencing on the Effective Date and ending on the Commercial Operation Date, Seller shall provide Buyer with quarterly written progress reports (each, a \"Progress Report\") within fifteen (15) days following the end of each calendar quarter. Each Progress Report shall include, at a minimum: (a) the status of major equipment procurement, including confirmation of turbine manufacturing and delivery schedules with Nordex; (b) a summary of construction milestones achieved during the preceding quarter, with reference to the milestone schedule set forth in Exhibit G; (c) an updated construction schedule identifying any changes from the prior quarter; (d) a description of any anticipated delays in achieving any milestone or the Expected COD, including the nature and cause of such delay and Seller\'s proposed mitigation measures; and (e) such other information as Buyer may reasonably request. Progress Reports are for informational purposes only and shall not modify, limit, or otherwise affect Seller\'s obligations under this Agreement.

**Section 3.5 --- Delay Liquidated Damages**

**Section 3.5(a) --- Accrual.** If Seller fails to achieve the Commercial Operation Date on or before the Guaranteed Commercial Operation Date, Seller shall pay to Buyer delay liquidated damages (\"Delay LDs\") for each month (or pro rata portion thereof) following the Guaranteed Commercial Operation Date until the earlier of (i) the date on which COD is achieved and (ii) the date of termination of this Agreement pursuant to Section 3.6 (the \"Termination Date\"). Delay LDs shall begin accruing on September 2, 2026 (the day following the Guaranteed Commercial Operation Date).

**Section 3.5(b) --- Delay LD Rate.** The Delay LD rate shall be One Hundred Seventy-Five Thousand Dollars (\$175,000) per month (or pro rata for any partial month). The Parties acknowledge and agree that the actual damages to Buyer resulting from a delay in achieving COD would be difficult or impossible to determine with precision, and the Delay LD rate set forth herein represents a reasonable estimate of the anticipated damages that Buyer would suffer as a result of such delay.

**Section 3.5(c) --- Aggregate Cap on Delay LDs.** Notwithstanding the foregoing, the aggregate amount of Delay LDs payable by Seller under this Section 3.5 shall not exceed Two Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$2,500,000) (the \"Delay LD Cap\"). Once the aggregate Delay LDs paid or payable by Seller equal the Delay LD Cap, no further Delay LDs shall accrue; provided, however, that the reaching of the Delay LD Cap shall not relieve Seller of its obligation to achieve COD by the Outside Date.

**Section 3.5(d) --- Payment.** Delay LDs shall be payable within thirty (30) days of Buyer\'s delivery of an invoice to Seller specifying the amount of Delay LDs due. At Buyer\'s election, Buyer may offset Delay LDs against any amounts otherwise owed by Buyer to Seller under this Agreement. The Parties acknowledge and agree that the payment of Delay LDs by Seller pursuant to this Section 3.5 shall constitute Seller\'s sole and exclusive liability, and Buyer\'s sole and exclusive remedy, for Seller\'s failure to achieve the Commercial Operation Date by the Guaranteed Commercial Operation Date, subject to Buyer\'s right to terminate this Agreement pursuant to Section 3.6.

**Section 3.6 --- Termination for Failure to Achieve COD**

If Seller fails to achieve the Commercial Operation Date by September 1, 2027 (the \"Outside Date\"), either Party may terminate this Agreement upon thirty (30) days\' written notice to the other Party, without further liability of either Party to the other except for (i) Delay LDs accrued prior to the effective date of termination, which shall remain payable in full, (ii) obligations under this Agreement that expressly survive termination, and (iii) the obligation of Seller to return or cause the release of any credit support provided by Buyer, if applicable. If neither Party delivers a termination notice within ninety (90) days following the Outside Date, the Outside Date shall be deemed extended by successive ninety (90) day periods until a Party exercises its right to terminate or COD is achieved.

**[ARTICLE 4 --- ENERGY PURCHASE AND SALE; PRICING]{.underline}**

**Section 4.1 --- Purchase and Sale Obligation**

During the Term, Seller shall sell and deliver, and Buyer shall purchase and receive, all of the Net Energy Output of the Facility delivered to the Delivery Point, subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement. The Parties acknowledge that the expected annual net generation at P50 is approximately eight hundred seventy-six thousand (876,000) MWh and that the \"Contract Quantity\" for purposes of this Agreement is eight hundred fifty thousand (850,000) MWh per Contract Year.

The \"Delivery Point\" shall mean the Southwest Power Pool (\"SPP\") node designated GEN-2205, being the point of interconnection for the Prairie Crest Wind Project at the high-voltage side of the project substation where the Facility interconnects with the SPP transmission system. All deliveries of energy under this Agreement shall occur at the Delivery Point, and Seller shall have no obligation to deliver energy at any point other than the Delivery Point.

The Parties acknowledge and agree that the Facility is a variable energy resource and that the actual Net Energy Output may vary from the Contract Quantity due to weather conditions, wind resource variability, and other factors. Subject to the curtailment provisions of Article 6 and the performance guarantee provisions of Article 8, Seller shall not be required to produce or deliver any minimum quantity of energy to Buyer, except as expressly set forth herein, and Buyer shall accept all Net Energy Output tendered by Seller at the Delivery Point during the Term. The obligation to purchase is an obligation to take and pay for energy as delivered and is not an obligation to purchase a specified volume of energy.

**Section 4.2 --- Contract Price**

**Section 4.2(a) --- Base Contract Price and Escalation.** The base contract price for energy delivered hereunder shall be Thirty-Eight Dollars and Fifty Cents (\$38.50) per MWh (the \"Base Contract Price\"), applicable during Contract Years 1 through 5. Beginning on the sixth (6th) anniversary of the Commercial Operation Date, the Contract Price shall escalate at a rate of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per annum, compounding annually (the \"Escalation Rate\"). The applicable Contract Price for each Contract Year shall be as set forth in the price table in Exhibit B.

The Parties acknowledge that the Base Contract Price and the Escalation Rate reflect the consideration negotiated between the Parties and take into account the expected performance of the Facility, current and projected wholesale energy market conditions in the SPP market, the value of Environmental Attributes and Renewable Energy Certificates to be transferred to Buyer, and the allocation of risks between the Parties under this Agreement. The Contract Price is a fixed price and shall not be subject to adjustment for changes in commodity prices, equipment costs, labor costs, or other market conditions, except as may be expressly provided in Article 14.

**Section 4.2(b) --- Calculation.** For each Contract Year n (where n is greater than or equal to 6), the Contract Price shall be calculated as follows:

Contract Price(n) = Base Contract Price × (1 + Escalation Rate)\^(n--5)

The resulting Contract Price shall be rounded to the nearest cent (\$0.01). A pre-computed table of the Contract Price for each Contract Year during the Term is set forth in Exhibit B, Part 2. In the event of any discrepancy between the formula in this Section 4.2(b) and the pre-computed table in Exhibit B, the provisions of Section 1.3 shall govern.

**Section 4.3 --- Invoicing and Payment**

\(a\) **Monthly Invoicing.** Within ten (10) Business Days after the end of each calendar month during the Term, Seller shall deliver to Buyer an invoice (each, a \"Monthly Invoice\") setting forth: (i) the total Net Energy Output (in MWh) delivered to the Delivery Point during such calendar month, as measured by the revenue meters in accordance with Article 7; (ii) the applicable Contract Price per MWh; (iii) the total amount due from Buyer for energy delivered; (iv) any adjustments for prior periods, including meter corrections; and (v) any amounts due from or owed to Buyer for curtailment compensation under Article 6 or liquidated damages under Article 8.

\(b\) **Payment.** Buyer shall pay the amount set forth in each Monthly Invoice within twenty (20) Business Days of receipt of such invoice. All payments shall be made by wire transfer of immediately available funds to the account designated by Seller in writing from time to time.

\(c\) **Late Payment.** Any amounts not paid when due shall bear interest from the date due until the date paid at a rate equal to the lower of (i) one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month (eighteen percent (18%) per annum) and (ii) the maximum rate permitted by Applicable Law. Payment of interest shall not excuse or cure any default by Buyer.

\(d\) **Disputed Amounts.** If Buyer in good faith disputes any amount set forth in a Monthly Invoice, Buyer shall pay the undisputed portion of such invoice when due and shall provide Seller with a written statement of the disputed amount and the basis for such dispute within the twenty (20) Business Day payment period. The Parties shall use commercially reasonable efforts to resolve any billing dispute within thirty (30) days. If the Parties are unable to resolve such dispute, either Party may invoke the dispute resolution procedures set forth in Article 19. Any amounts determined to be owed following resolution of a dispute shall be paid within ten (10) Business Days of such resolution, together with interest thereon at the rate specified in clause (c) above.

**Section 4.4 --- Netting**

If, on any date, both Buyer and Seller owe amounts to the other under this Agreement, then the amounts owed by each Party may be netted against each other, and the Party owing the larger aggregate amount shall pay to the other Party the net difference. Netting shall apply to all amounts due under this Agreement, including energy payments, curtailment compensation, liquidated damages, and interest. Nothing in this Section 4.4 shall relieve either Party of its obligation to timely dispute any invoice or payment.

**[ARTICLE 5 --- DELIVERY AND TITLE TRANSFER]{.underline}**

**Section 5.1 --- Delivery Point**

All energy produced by the Facility and delivered to Buyer under this Agreement shall be delivered at the Delivery Point (SPP node GEN-2205), which is the point of interconnection between the Facility and the SPP transmission system at the high-voltage side of the project substation. Title to and risk of loss of all electric energy shall pass from Seller to Buyer at the Delivery Point. Prior to the Delivery Point, Seller shall bear all risk of loss with respect to such energy, and from and after the Delivery Point, Buyer shall bear all risk of loss with respect to such energy. Neither Party shall be responsible for the acts or omissions of the other Party occurring on such other Party\'s side of the Delivery Point.

**Section 5.2 --- Seller\'s Delivery Obligations**

Seller shall be responsible for all costs, charges, losses, and arrangements necessary to deliver the Net Energy Output of the Facility to the Delivery Point, including: (a) all costs associated with the Facility\'s interconnection to the SPP transmission system, including the costs of interconnection facilities and network upgrades as specified in the Large Generator Interconnection Agreement; (b) all station service and auxiliary loads consumed by the Facility in the production of electric energy; (c) all electrical losses occurring between the generator terminals and the Delivery Point, including collector system losses and transformation losses within the project substation; and (d) all costs of maintaining the Large Generator Interconnection Agreement in full force and effect. Seller shall at all times maintain its SPP market participant registration and comply with all applicable SPP market rules and reliability standards in

connection with the operation of the Facility and the delivery of energy to the Delivery Point.

**Section 5.3 --- Buyer\'s Receipt Obligations**

Buyer shall be responsible for all costs, charges, losses, and arrangements necessary from and after the Delivery Point, including: (a) all transmission charges and ancillary service charges imposed by SPP or any transmission provider for the transmission of energy from the Delivery Point to Buyer\'s load; (b) all scheduling and balancing costs incurred in connection with the receipt and delivery of energy beyond the Delivery Point; and (c) all electrical losses occurring beyond the Delivery Point. Buyer shall at all times maintain firm or non-firm transmission service from the Delivery Point to its load, as Buyer deems appropriate.

**Section 5.4 --- Scheduling**

Seller shall submit energy schedules to SPP for the Facility in accordance with SPP market rules and the SPP Open Access Transmission Tariff. Seller shall provide Buyer with day-ahead forecasts of expected generation for each operating day, updated not less than two (2) hours prior to the start of each operating hour. The Parties shall cooperate in good faith to minimize imbalance charges and to optimize the scheduling and dispatch of the Facility\'s output within the SPP market framework. To the extent that any imbalance charges are assessed by SPP in connection with the Facility\'s output, such charges shall be allocated between the Parties in accordance with the applicable provisions of the SPP Open Access Transmission Tariff; provided, however, that Seller shall be responsible for imbalance charges attributable to inaccurate generation forecasts by Seller to the extent such inaccuracy exceeds the tolerances set forth in the SPP market rules.

**[ARTICLE 6 --- CURTAILMENT]{.underline}**

**Section 6.1 --- Types of Curtailment**

For purposes of this Agreement, \"Curtailment\" means any reduction, interruption, or cessation of the generation or delivery of energy from the Facility that would otherwise have been generated and delivered to the Delivery Point absent the curtailing event. Curtailment shall be classified into three categories:

\(a\) **\"Economic Curtailment\"** means any Curtailment initiated at the direction of Buyer or Buyer\'s designee (including Buyer\'s balancing authority or scheduling agent) for economic reasons, including but not limited to periods during which the SPP locational marginal price at the Delivery Point is negative or below a threshold agreed by the Parties, or periods during which Buyer determines that acceptance of energy from the Facility would not be economically beneficial to Buyer or its customers.

\(b\) **\"System Curtailment\"** means any Curtailment required by SPP, any reliability coordinator, or any transmission provider for reliability, congestion management, system emergency, or similar operational reasons, including curtailments resulting from transmission outages, system voltage support requirements, or minimum generation events, in each case that are not initiated at the direction of Buyer.

\(c\) **\"Seller Curtailment\"** means any Curtailment initiated by Seller for its own operational, maintenance, or commercial reasons, including planned maintenance outages, unplanned equipment failures, environmental compliance activities, and any other curtailment not constituting Economic Curtailment or System Curtailment.

**Section 6.2 --- Curtailment Compensation**

**Section 6.2(a) --- Economic Curtailment Compensation.** In the event of Economic Curtailment, Buyer shall compensate Seller for energy that would have been generated and delivered to the Delivery Point but for such curtailment, at a rate equal to eighty percent (80%) of the then-applicable Contract Price per MWh of curtailed energy, as measured by the Facility\'s SCADA system and verified in accordance with Section 6.3. The amount of curtailed energy for purposes of this Section 6.2(a) shall be determined by calculating the difference between the energy that the Facility would have produced under prevailing wind conditions (as determined in accordance with Section 6.3) and the energy actually produced during the period of Economic Curtailment. Buyer shall pay compensation for Economic Curtailment as part of the monthly invoicing and payment process set forth in Section 4.3.

**Section 6.2(b) --- System Curtailment.** No compensation shall be payable by either Party in connection with System Curtailment. System Curtailment shall be treated as a Force Majeure event for purposes of the performance guarantee calculations set forth in Article 8, and energy that would have been generated but for System Curtailment shall be excluded from the calculation of any shortfall under Section 8.3 and Section 8.4.

**Section 6.2(c) --- Seller Curtailment.** No compensation shall be payable by Buyer in connection with Seller Curtailment. Any energy that would have been generated but for Seller Curtailment shall not be excluded from the calculation of Net Energy Output for purposes of the performance guarantees set forth in Article 8, and Seller Curtailment shall be counted against Seller\'s Minimum Annual Energy Production guarantee.

**Section 6.3 --- Curtailment Measurement**

The quantity of energy curtailed during any Curtailment event shall be calculated based on the Facility\'s supervisory control and data acquisition (\"SCADA\") system data using the following methodology: (a) for each turbine subject to the Curtailment, the nacelle anemometer wind speed readings recorded during the period of Curtailment shall be applied to the manufacturer\'s warranted power curve for the Nordex Delta4000 turbine, adjusted for actual grid voltage and ambient temperature as recorded by the Facility\'s meteorological stations; (b) the resulting calculated energy production for each turbine shall be aggregated and reduced by the applicable station service and loss factor (as determined in accordance with Exhibit C) to derive the estimated Net Energy Output that would have been delivered to the Delivery Point; and (c) the curtailed energy shall be the difference between such estimated Net Energy Output and the actual Net Energy Output delivered to the Delivery Point during the Curtailment period. In the event of a dispute regarding the calculation of curtailed energy, either Party may invoke the dispute resolution procedures set forth in Article 19.

**Section 6.4 --- Annual Curtailment Cap**

Buyer\'s obligation to compensate Seller for Economic Curtailment under Section 6.2(a) shall be limited to an aggregate of forty-two thousand five hundred (42,500) MWh per Contract Year (equal to five percent (5%) of the Contract Quantity). Economic Curtailment in excess of such cap shall not be compensated. For the avoidance of doubt, this cap applies only to the compensation obligation; Buyer retains the right to direct Economic Curtailment in excess of the cap, but Seller shall have no obligation to accept uncompensated Economic Curtailment that exceeds the cap unless required by Applicable Law or SPP directives.

**[ARTICLE 7 --- METERING]{.underline}**

**Section 7.1 --- Metering Equipment**

Seller shall install, own, operate, and maintain, at its sole cost and expense, revenue-grade metering equipment at the Delivery Point in accordance with the specifications and requirements set forth in Exhibit D. Such metering equipment shall meet the accuracy standards of ANSI C12.20 (0.2% accuracy class) and shall be capable of measuring and recording the quantity of energy delivered to the Delivery Point in fifteen (15) minute intervals. Seller shall ensure that the metering equipment is compatible with SPP market settlement systems and complies with SPP metering standards. Buyer shall have the right, at Buyer\'s sole cost and expense, to install, own, operate, and maintain check meters at or near the Delivery Point for purposes of verifying the accuracy of the revenue meters. The revenue meters maintained by Seller shall be the primary meters for purposes of billing and payment under this Agreement. In the event of a discrepancy between the revenue meters and the check meters exceeding the tolerance specified in Exhibit D, Section 5, either Party may request a special meter test in accordance with Section 7.2.

**Section 7.2 --- Meter Testing and Calibration**

Seller shall cause the revenue meters at the Delivery Point to be tested and calibrated at least once per calendar year by a qualified, independent testing organization. Such annual testing shall be conducted in accordance with the testing protocols set forth in Exhibit D, Section 5. If any revenue meter is found to be inaccurate by more than plus or minus one-half percent (±0.5%), the meter readings shall be adjusted for billing purposes for the lesser of (a) the period during which the meter is determined to have been inaccurate (if such period can be reasonably determined) and (b) ninety (90) days prior to the date on which the inaccuracy was discovered. If the period of inaccuracy cannot be determined, the adjustment shall be for the ninety (90) day period. The adjusted amounts shall be reflected in the next Monthly Invoice following the determination of the adjustment. Either Party may request a special meter test at any time by providing written notice to the other Party, with the cost of such special test borne by the requesting Party unless the meter is found to be inaccurate by more than ±0.5%, in which case the cost shall be borne by Seller.

**Section 7.3 --- Data Sharing**

Seller shall provide Buyer with real-time access to metering data from the revenue meters at the Delivery Point via a secure electronic interface, in a format reasonably acceptable to Buyer. Additionally, Seller shall deliver to Buyer monthly meter data reports within five (5) Business Days after the end of each calendar month, summarizing the aggregate energy delivered during such month, daily and hourly generation profiles, and any meter outages or data gaps that occurred during the period.

**[ARTICLE 8 --- PERFORMANCE GUARANTEES AND LIQUIDATED DAMAGES]{.underline}**

**Section 8.1 --- General**

Seller guarantees the performance of the Facility in accordance with the standards set forth in this Article 8. The Parties acknowledge and agree that the liquidated damages set forth in this Article 8 are a reasonable estimate of the damages that Buyer would suffer as a result of the applicable performance shortfalls and represent Buyer\'s sole and exclusive remedy for such shortfalls, except for Buyer\'s termination rights under Article 18. Nothing in this Article 8 shall limit Buyer\'s rights under any other provision of this Agreement.

**Section 8.2 --- Annual Energy Production Measurement**

For purposes of measuring Seller\'s performance against the guarantees set forth in this Article 8, the Net Energy Output delivered to the Delivery Point during each Contract Year shall be measured by the revenue meters installed and maintained in accordance with Article 7. In calculating the Net Energy Output for purposes of the performance guarantees, the following adjustments shall be made:

\(a\) Energy that would have been delivered to the Delivery Point but for System Curtailment (as defined in Section 6.1(b)) shall be added to the actual metered Net Energy Output for purposes of determining compliance with the Minimum Annual Energy Production guarantee;

\(b\) Energy that would have been delivered to the Delivery Point but for a Force Majeure event (as defined in Article 12) shall be added to the actual metered Net Energy Output for purposes of determining compliance with the Minimum Annual Energy Production guarantee;

\(c\) Energy that was not delivered due to Buyer\'s failure to perform its obligations under this Agreement (including Buyer-caused outages or delays) shall be added to the actual metered Net Energy Output for purposes of determining compliance with the Minimum Annual Energy Production guarantee; and

\(d\) Energy that was not delivered due to Economic Curtailment shall be added to the actual metered Net Energy Output for purposes of determining compliance with the Minimum Annual Energy Production guarantee.

**Section 8.3 --- Minimum Annual Energy Production Guarantee**

Seller guarantees that the Net Energy Output delivered to the Delivery Point during each Contract Year, as adjusted in accordance with Section 8.2, shall equal or exceed seventy-five percent (75%) of the Contract Quantity (the \"Minimum Annual Energy Production\" or \"MAEP\"). For the avoidance of doubt, the MAEP equals 637,500 MWh (being 75% of 850,000 MWh). The Parties acknowledge that the MAEP represents a reasonable minimum performance threshold for the Facility, taking into account expected wind resource variability and the operating characteristics of the Nordex Delta4000 wind turbine generators.

**Section 8.4 --- Performance Shortfall Liquidated Damages**

If the Net Energy Output delivered during any Contract Year, as adjusted in accordance with Section 8.2, is less than the MAEP, Seller shall pay to Buyer performance shortfall liquidated damages (\"Shortfall LDs\") calculated as follows:

Shortfall LDs = (MAEP -- Actual Adjusted Net Energy Output) × 50% × Contract Price(applicable)

For the avoidance of doubt, the Shortfall LD rate is fifty percent (50%) of the then-applicable Contract Price per MWh of deficit below the MAEP. By way of illustration, if in Contract Year 1 the Actual Adjusted Net Energy Output is 600,000 MWh, the Shortfall LDs would be calculated as: (637,500 -- 600,000) × 50% × \$38.50 = \$721,875.

Shortfall LDs for each Contract Year shall be calculated within sixty (60) days following the end of such Contract Year and shall be invoiced by Buyer and payable by Seller within thirty (30) days of such invoice. The Parties acknowledge and agree that the actual damages arising from a production shortfall would be difficult or impossible to determine with precision, and the Shortfall LD rate set forth herein represents a reasonable estimate of such damages.

**Section 8.5 --- Shortfall LD Cap**

The aggregate Shortfall LDs payable by Seller during any single Contract Year shall not exceed an amount equal to twenty percent (20%) of the annual revenue for such Contract Year (calculated as the Contract Quantity multiplied by the applicable Contract Price for such Contract Year). Shortfall LDs are Buyer\'s sole and exclusive remedy for production shortfalls below the MAEP, except for Buyer\'s termination rights under Article 18 in the event of repeated material shortfalls constituting a material breach.

**Section 8.6 --- Excess Energy**

If the Net Energy Output delivered to the Delivery Point during any Contract Year exceeds the Contract Quantity, Buyer shall purchase such excess energy at the applicable Contract Price. There shall be no carry-over of excess energy production credits from one Contract Year to any subsequent Contract Year, and excess production in one Contract Year shall not be applied to offset shortfalls in any prior or subsequent Contract Year.

**Section 8.7 --- Mechanical Availability Guarantee**

Seller guarantees that the Facility shall achieve a Mechanical Availability of at least ninety-five percent (95%) during each Contract Year (the \"Guaranteed Mechanical Availability\"). \"Mechanical Availability\" shall be calculated as set forth in Exhibit C, Section 3. In computing Mechanical Availability, periods of System Curtailment, Force Majeure events, Buyer-caused outages, and planned maintenance conducted in accordance with an approved maintenance schedule (per Section 9.2) shall be excluded from both the numerator and the denominator of the availability calculation.

If the actual Mechanical Availability during any Contract Year falls below ninety-five percent (95%), Seller shall pay to Buyer mechanical availability liquidated damages (\"Availability LDs\") equal to Sixty-Five Thousand Dollars (\$65,000) per percentage point (or pro rata fraction thereof) by which actual Mechanical Availability falls below the Guaranteed Mechanical Availability. By way of illustration, if actual Mechanical Availability during a Contract Year is 93%, Seller shall pay 2.0 × \$65,000 = \$130,000 in Availability LDs for such Contract Year.

Availability LDs shall be calculated and invoiced in the same manner as Shortfall LDs under Section 8.4 and shall be payable within thirty (30) days of invoice. Availability LDs shall be in addition to, and not in lieu of, Shortfall LDs, to the extent both are applicable; provided, however, that in no event shall Seller be required to pay both Shortfall LDs and Availability LDs with respect to the same energy deficit (i.e., to the extent that a production shortfall is attributable to mechanical unavailability, the deficit giving rise to Availability LDs shall be excluded from the calculation of Shortfall LDs to avoid double recovery).

**Section 8.8 --- Measurement Period Adjustments**

If the first Contract Year or the last Contract Year is less than twelve (12) full months, the MAEP, Contract Quantity, curtailment cap, and other annual performance benchmarks shall be prorated on a daily basis to reflect the actual number of days in such partial Contract Year. In addition, the performance guarantee thresholds shall be adjusted for Force Majeure events, System Curtailment, and Buyer-caused outages to the extent provided in Section 8.2. The Parties shall cooperate in good faith to determine the appropriate adjustments for each affected Contract Year.

**[ARTICLE 9 --- OPERATIONS AND MAINTENANCE]{.underline}**

**Section 9.1 --- Operating Standards**

Seller shall operate and maintain the Facility at all times in accordance with Prudent Utility Practice, the turbine manufacturer\'s operation and maintenance guidelines for the Nordex Delta4000 wind turbine generators, and all Applicable Laws, governmental permits, and regulatory requirements. Seller shall comply with all applicable reliability standards promulgated by the North American Electric Reliability Corporation, the SPP Regional Entity, and any applicable governmental authority. Seller shall maintain a qualified and experienced operations team responsible for the day-to-day operation of the Facility and shall ensure that all maintenance personnel have been properly trained on the Nordex Delta4000 platform.

**Section 9.2 --- Maintenance Schedule**

Seller shall prepare and deliver to Buyer an annual maintenance schedule for the Facility by December 1 of each calendar year during the Term. Such schedule shall identify all planned maintenance activities anticipated during the following calendar year, including estimated durations and the number of turbines expected to be offline during each planned maintenance period. To the extent practicable, Seller shall schedule planned maintenance outages during periods of historically lower wind resource (typically June through September in Osage County, Oklahoma). Seller shall provide Buyer with not less than thirty (30) days\' prior written notice of any planned outage expected to exceed forty-eight (48) hours in duration. Seller shall use commercially reasonable efforts to minimize the impact of planned maintenance on Net Energy Output.

**Section 9.3 --- Staffing**

Seller shall maintain qualified operations and maintenance personnel at or near the Facility site at all times during the Term. Seller shall designate a plant manager (or equivalent) and shall provide Buyer with the name and contact information for such plant manager. Buyer and its authorized representatives shall have reasonable access to the Facility for the purpose of inspection and observation, upon not less than forty-eight (48) hours\' prior written notice to Seller (or shorter notice in the case of an emergency), subject to Seller\'s reasonable safety and security requirements.

**Section 9.4 --- Environmental Compliance**

Seller shall be solely responsible for compliance with all environmental laws, permits, and conditions applicable to the Facility, including the Clean Air Act, the Clean Water Act, the Endangered Species Act, the National Environmental Policy Act, and all applicable Oklahoma environmental statutes and regulations. Seller shall maintain a bird and bat monitoring program as required by the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service and the Oklahoma Department of Wildlife Conservation, and shall promptly notify Buyer of any material environmental compliance issues or permit violations at the Facility.

**[ARTICLE 10 --- ENVIRONMENTAL ATTRIBUTES AND RENEWABLE ENERGY CERTIFICATES]{.underline}**

**Section 10.1 --- Ownership of Environmental Attributes**

All Environmental Attributes, including Renewable Energy Certificates (\"RECs\"), associated with the Net Energy Output delivered by Seller to Buyer up to and including one hundred percent (100%) of the Contract Quantity in any Contract Year shall be owned by and transferred to Buyer, bundled with the energy. Such Environmental Attributes shall be deemed transferred to Buyer at the Delivery Point simultaneously with the delivery of the associated energy, and Seller shall take all actions and execute all documents reasonably necessary to effectuate such transfer. For the avoidance of doubt, Environmental Attributes and RECs associated with Net Energy Output in excess of one hundred percent (100%) of the Contract Quantity in any Contract Year shall be retained by Seller and shall not transfer to Buyer. Seller shall have the right to market, sell, trade, or retire such excess Environmental Attributes and RECs in its sole discretion.

\"Environmental Attributes\" means any and all fuel, emissions, air quality, or other environmental-related credits, benefits, emissions reductions, offsets, and allowances, howsoever entitled, attributable to the generation of electric energy from the Facility, including Renewable Energy Certificates, green tags, tradeable renewable credits, carbon credits, emissions allowances, and any similar attributes created by or arising under any federal, state, regional, or voluntary program or market, whether existing now or in the future. The Parties intend that Buyer shall receive and be entitled to claim the full environmental benefit associated with the renewable energy purchased under this Agreement, up to the Contract Quantity.

**Section 10.2 --- REC Registration and Transfer**

Seller shall register all RECs generated by the Facility with the Midwest Renewable Energy Tracking System (\"M-RETS\") or any successor tracking system designated by Buyer. Within sixty (60) days following the end of each calendar month during which Net Energy Output was delivered, Seller shall cause the RECs associated with such Net Energy Output (up to the Contract Quantity, on a cumulative annual basis) to be transferred to Buyer\'s M-RETS account (or such other account as Buyer may designate). Seller shall cooperate with Buyer in connection with Buyer\'s renewable portfolio standard (\"RPS\") compliance filings, green power certifications, and similar reporting obligations, including by providing such documentation and certifications as Buyer may reasonably request.

**Section 10.3 --- Qualification**

Seller shall, at its own expense, obtain and maintain throughout the Term the qualification of the Facility as an eligible renewable energy resource under Oklahoma law and under any applicable state RPS programs in effect in Buyer\'s member municipalities or any other jurisdiction in which Buyer seeks to apply the Environmental Attributes acquired hereunder. Seller shall promptly notify Buyer of any change in the qualification status of the Facility.

**Section 10.4 --- Tax Credits**

All federal and state tax credits, benefits, deductions, and incentives arising from the construction, ownership, and operation of the Facility, including Production Tax Credits under Section 45 of the Internal Revenue Code, Investment Tax Credits under Section 48 of the Internal Revenue Code, and any successor or replacement tax incentives, shall be retained by Seller. Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed to transfer, assign, or convey any tax benefit from Seller to Buyer.

**[ARTICLE 11 --- REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES]{.underline}**

**Section 11.1 --- Seller\'s Representations and Warranties**

Seller represents and warrants to Buyer, as of the Effective Date, and shall be deemed to repeat each of the following representations and warranties on the Commercial Operation Date, that:

\(a\) Seller is a limited liability company duly organized, validly existing, and in good standing under the laws of the State of Delaware, formed on February 12, 2023, and is duly qualified to do business and in good standing in the State of Oklahoma. Seller\'s Employer Identification Number is 92-4187563.

\(b\) Seller has all necessary limited liability company power and authority to execute, deliver, and perform this Agreement and to consummate the transactions contemplated hereby. The execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement by Seller have been duly and validly authorized by all requisite limited liability company action on the part of Seller.

\(c\) The execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement by Seller do not and will not: (i) violate or conflict with the certificate of formation, limited liability company agreement, or other organizational documents of Seller; (ii) violate or conflict with, or result in a breach of, or constitute a default under, any material agreement, instrument, or obligation to which Seller is a party or by which Seller or its assets are bound; or (iii) violate or conflict with any Applicable Law applicable to Seller.

\(d\) There is no action, suit, proceeding, or investigation pending or, to Seller\'s knowledge, threatened against Seller that would reasonably be expected to have a material adverse effect on Seller\'s ability to perform its obligations under this Agreement.

\(e\) This Agreement constitutes the valid and binding obligation of Seller, enforceable against Seller in accordance with its terms, subject to applicable bankruptcy, insolvency, reorganization, moratorium, and similar laws affecting creditors\' rights generally and to general principles of equity.

\(f\) Seller has obtained, or is in the process of obtaining, all material permits, licenses, and governmental approvals required for the development, construction, and operation of the Facility, and Seller is not aware of any circumstances that would prevent or materially delay the issuance of any such permit, license, or approval.

\(g\) Seller is a wholly owned subsidiary of Verdana Renewable Holdings Inc., a Delaware corporation, and no other Person holds any ownership interest in Seller.

\(h\) Seller is not, and upon completion of the Facility will not be, a \"public utility\" as defined under the laws of the State of Oklahoma.

\(i\) All factual information provided by Seller to Buyer in connection with the negotiation of this Agreement was, to Seller\'s knowledge, true and correct in all material respects as of the date such information was provided.

**Section 11.2 --- Buyer\'s Representations and Warranties**

Buyer represents and warrants to Seller, as of the Effective Date, that:

\(a\) Buyer is a municipal electric utility duly organized and validly existing under Title 11, Chapter 30 of the Oklahoma Municipal Power Act, with full power and authority to own and operate its utility system and to provide electric service to its customers within its service territory. Buyer\'s Employer Identification Number is 73-0285941.
