\(g\) Buyer has been duly authorized by its governing body to enter into this Agreement for a term of twenty (20) Contract Years, and such authorization has been obtained in compliance with all Applicable Laws, including any public meeting or open records requirements.

**Section 11.3 --- Survival**

The representations and warranties set forth in this Article 11 shall survive the execution and delivery of this Agreement and shall remain in full force and effect throughout the Term and for a period of twelve (12) months following the expiration or termination of this Agreement.

**[ARTICLE 12 --- FORCE MAJEURE]{.underline}**

**Section 12.1 --- Definition**

\"Force Majeure\" means any event or circumstance beyond the reasonable control of the affected Party that prevents or delays performance of such Party\'s obligations under this Agreement, including: acts of God; fire; flood; earthquake; tornado; hurricane; severe storm; ice storm; lightning; epidemic or pandemic; war (whether declared or undeclared); terrorism; sabotage; civil unrest; insurrection; riot; blockade; embargo; labor strikes, lockouts, or work stoppages (other than labor strikes, lockouts, or work stoppages involving Seller\'s own employees or contractors at the Facility); actions of any governmental authority (including changes in Applicable Law, denial or revocation of permits, or government-imposed moratoriums); failure of the SPP transmission system (to the extent not caused by the affected Party); and severe weather conditions that prevent construction or operation of the Facility.

Notwithstanding the foregoing, Force Majeure shall not include: (a) economic hardship, including changes in Seller\'s costs of performing its obligations hereunder; (b) changes in market prices for energy, capacity, environmental attributes, or commodities; (c) Seller\'s inability to obtain or maintain financing for the Facility; (d) equipment or labor shortages that could have been avoided through commercially reasonable planning and procurement practices; (e) Seller\'s failure to timely apply for or obtain permits that could have been obtained through the exercise of reasonable diligence; or (f) normal wear and tear or equipment degradation.

**Section 12.2 --- Notice**

The Party claiming Force Majeure (the \"Affected Party\") shall provide written notice to the other Party within five (5) Business Days of becoming aware of the Force Majeure event. Such notice shall include: (a) a description of the Force Majeure event and the obligations affected thereby; (b) the expected duration of the Force Majeure event; (c) a description of the steps being taken or proposed to be taken by the Affected Party to mitigate the effects of the Force Majeure event; and (d) an estimated date for the resumption of performance. The Affected Party shall provide updated notices as the circumstances warrant.

**Section 12.3 --- Effect**

Neither Party shall be liable to the other Party for any failure or delay in performance to the extent caused by a Force Majeure event, provided that the Affected Party has complied with the notice requirements of Section 12.2 and is using commercially reasonable efforts to mitigate the effects of the Force Majeure event and to resume performance as promptly as practicable. The non-affected Party\'s obligations to make payments for energy already delivered prior to the Force Majeure event shall not be suspended. During the continuance of a Force Majeure event, the Affected Party shall continue to perform all obligations not affected by the Force Majeure event. The occurrence of a Force Majeure event shall not extend the Term of this Agreement, except as may be otherwise provided in Section 3.5 with respect to the Guaranteed COD and Delay LDs.

**Section 12.4 --- Termination for Extended Force Majeure**

If a Force Majeure event continues for a period of twelve (12) consecutive months, either Party may terminate this Agreement upon sixty (60) days\' written notice to the other Party, without further liability to either Party (except for obligations accrued prior to the effective date of termination, including amounts payable for energy delivered prior to the Force Majeure event and Delay LDs accrued prior to the Force Majeure event, and obligations that expressly survive termination pursuant to this Agreement). Upon such termination, Seller shall return or cause the release of any credit support then held by Buyer, and Buyer shall pay all amounts due for energy delivered prior to the termination.

**[ARTICLE 13 --- CREDIT SUPPORT]{.underline}**

**Section 13.1 --- Seller\'s Credit Support**

Within thirty (30) days of the Effective Date, Seller shall deliver to Buyer a performance bond in the amount of Seven Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$7,500,000) (the \"Performance Bond\") issued by a surety company rated at least A-- by Atlas Credit Services. The form of Performance Bond is attached as Exhibit F. The Performance Bond shall name Lakeshore Municipal Electric Authority as obligee and Crescent Ridge Wind Partners LLC as principal. The expected surety issuer is Highpoint Surety & Hartleigh Co.

The Performance Bond shall remain in effect throughout the Term of this Agreement and shall be renewable annually. Seller shall provide evidence of the renewal of the Performance Bond to Buyer at least thirty (30) days prior to the expiration of the then-current bond period. If at any time the surety issuing the Performance Bond is downgraded below A-- by Atlas Credit Services, Seller shall replace the Performance Bond with a bond from a surety rated at least A-- by Atlas Credit Services within thirty (30) days of such downgrade. If Seller fails to maintain the Performance Bond in accordance with this Section 13.1, such failure shall constitute an Event of Default under Section 18.1.

**Section 13.2 --- Buyer\'s Credit Support**

In light of Buyer\'s status as an investment-grade municipal electric utility with credit ratings of A2 by Sterling Ratings Agency and A by Atlas Credit Services, no credit support from Buyer shall be required under this Agreement as of the Effective Date. The absence of Buyer credit support is based upon and conditional on Buyer maintaining at least one investment-grade credit rating from either Sterling Ratings Agency or Atlas Credit Services.

**Section 13.3 --- Downgrade Events**

If Buyer\'s credit rating is downgraded below investment grade by both Sterling Ratings Agency and Atlas Credit Services (i.e., below Baa3 by Sterling Ratings Agency and below BBB-- by Atlas Credit Services), Seller may, upon written notice to Buyer, request that Buyer provide cash collateral in an amount equal to three (3) months of expected revenue (calculated as one-quarter of the Contract Quantity multiplied by the then-applicable Contract Price). Buyer shall deliver such cash collateral within thirty (30) days of Seller\'s request. If at any time following a downgrade, Buyer\'s credit rating is restored to investment grade by at least one of such rating agencies, Seller shall promptly return the cash collateral to Buyer. Cash collateral shall be held in an interest-bearing escrow account at a mutually agreed commercial bank.

**[ARTICLE 14 --- CHANGE OF LAW]{.underline}**

**Section 14.1 --- General**

Each Party shall comply with all Applicable Laws in effect from time to time. Except as otherwise provided in this Article 14, the adoption, modification, or repeal of any Applicable Law after the Effective Date shall not excuse either Party from its obligations hereunder. Each Party shall be responsible for obtaining and maintaining all regulatory approvals, licenses, and permits required for such Party\'s performance under this Agreement.

**Section 14.2 --- Allocation of Increased Costs**

If any change in Applicable Law enacted, adopted, or implemented after the Effective Date results in a material increase in the cost to either Party of performing its obligations under this Agreement, each Party shall bear its own increased costs arising from such change in Applicable Law. For purposes of this Section 14.2, a \"material increase\" means an increase in the annual cost of performance by more than Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$500,000) per Contract Year. The Parties shall, at the request of either Party, negotiate in good faith to determine whether any adjustment to the terms of this Agreement is appropriate to address the impact of such change in Applicable Law; provided, however, that neither Party shall be obligated to agree to any such adjustment. Nothing in this Section 14.2 shall relieve either Party of its obligation to perform under this Agreement as a result of changes in Applicable Law, and the failure to reach agreement on any adjustment shall not constitute a default or excuse non-performance by either Party.

**Section 14.3 --- Regulatory Approvals**

Each Party shall be responsible for obtaining and maintaining, at its own cost and expense, all regulatory approvals, licenses, and permits required for the performance of its obligations under this Agreement. The Parties shall cooperate in good faith with respect to any regulatory proceedings or governmental actions that may affect the rights or obligations of either Party under this Agreement, including by providing testimony, documentation, and other support as may be reasonably requested by the other Party.

**[ARTICLE 15 --- INSURANCE]{.underline}**

**Section 15.1 --- Required Insurance**

Seller shall obtain and maintain, at its sole cost and expense, throughout the Term of this Agreement (and during the construction period, as applicable), the following insurance coverages, each in accordance with the requirements set forth in Exhibit E:

\(a\) **Commercial General Liability Insurance.** Coverage for bodily injury and property damage with a combined single limit of not less than Five Million Dollars (\$5,000,000) per occurrence.

\(b\) **Pollution Liability Insurance.** Coverage for pollution conditions arising from the construction and operation of the Facility with a limit of not less than Two Million Dollars (\$2,000,000) per occurrence.

\(c\) **Builder\'s Risk Insurance (Construction Period Only).** Coverage for physical loss or damage to the Facility during the construction period, in an amount equal to the full replacement value of the Facility.

\(d\) **Workers\' Compensation and Employer\'s Liability Insurance.** Workers\' Compensation coverage at statutory limits and Employer\'s Liability coverage with a limit of not less than One Million Dollars (\$1,000,000) per occurrence.

\(e\) **Property Insurance (Operational Period).** All-risk property coverage for the Facility in an amount equal to the full replacement value of the Facility.

\(f\) **Business Interruption Insurance.** Coverage for loss of revenue resulting from physical damage to the Facility, in an amount sufficient to cover at least twelve (12) months of projected revenue.

All insurance policies required hereunder shall be issued by carriers rated at least A-- by Atlas Credit Services. Buyer shall be named as an additional insured on the Commercial General Liability and Property Insurance policies. All policies shall provide for a waiver of subrogation in favor of Buyer in accordance with Section 15.3.

**Section 15.2 --- Evidence of Insurance**

Seller shall deliver to Buyer certificates of insurance evidencing all required coverages prior to the commencement of construction of the Facility and annually thereafter by January 31 of each calendar year. Such certificates shall identify the coverages, limits, deductibles, and carriers, and shall confirm that Buyer is named as an additional insured where required. Seller shall provide Buyer with not less than thirty (30) days\' prior written notice of any cancellation, non-renewal, or material modification of any required insurance policy.

**Section 15.3 --- Waiver of Subrogation**

Each Party waives all rights of recovery and subrogation against the other Party and its Affiliates, officers, directors, employees, and agents, to the extent that any loss or damage is covered (or would have been covered had such Party maintained the insurance required hereunder) by any insurance policy maintained by such Party.

**Section 16.1 --- Mutual Indemnification**

Each Party (the \"Indemnifying Party\") shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the other Party, its Affiliates, and their respective officers, directors, employees, agents, successors, and permitted assigns (collectively, the \"Indemnified Parties\") from and against any and all third-party claims, demands, suits, actions, proceedings, judgments, damages, losses, liabilities, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees and court costs) (collectively, \"Losses\") arising out of or relating to: (a) bodily injury or death of any Person; (b) damage to or destruction of property of any Person; or (c) violation of any Applicable Law by the Indemnifying Party, in each case to the extent caused by the negligence, gross negligence, or willful misconduct of the Indemnifying Party or its agents, employees, contractors, or subcontractors in connection with the performance of this Agreement.

The Indemnified Party shall promptly notify the Indemnifying Party of any claim for which indemnification is sought and shall cooperate in the defense thereof. The Indemnifying Party shall have the right to control the defense and settlement of any such claim, provided that the Indemnifying Party shall not settle any claim without the prior written consent of the Indemnified Party (which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld) if such settlement would impose any obligation or restriction on the Indemnified Party or result in any admission of liability by the Indemnified Party.

**Section 16.2 --- Limitation of Liability**

EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT, NEITHER PARTY SHALL BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER PARTY FOR ANY CONSEQUENTIAL, INCIDENTAL, PUNITIVE, EXEMPLARY, OR INDIRECT DAMAGES, LOST PROFITS, OR LOSS OF BUSINESS OPPORTUNITY, WHETHER ARISING IN CONTRACT, TORT (INCLUDING NEGLIGENCE), STRICT LIABILITY, OR OTHERWISE, REGARDLESS OF WHETHER SUCH DAMAGES WERE FORESEEABLE OR WHETHER SUCH PARTY WAS ADVISED OF THE POSSIBILITY THEREOF; PROVIDED, HOWEVER, THAT THIS LIMITATION SHALL NOT APPLY TO: (A) A PARTY\'S INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS UNDER SECTION 16.1; (B) DAMAGES ARISING FROM A PARTY\'S WILLFUL MISCONDUCT OR FRAUD; OR (C) LIQUIDATED DAMAGES EXPRESSLY PROVIDED FOR UNDER THIS AGREEMENT.

**Section 16.3 --- Aggregate Liability Cap**

The aggregate liability of either Party arising under or in connection with this Agreement (excluding indemnification obligations for third-party bodily injury or death under Section 16.1 and liability for willful misconduct or fraud) shall not exceed the aggregate Contract Price payable during the Term, calculated as the Contract Quantity multiplied by the applicable Contract Price for each Contract Year, summed over all Contract Years of the Term.

**[ARTICLE 17 --- ASSIGNMENT]{.underline}**

**Section 17.1 --- Assignment by Seller**

**Section 17.1(a) --- Collateral Assignment to Financing Parties.** Seller may, without the prior consent of Buyer, collaterally assign its rights and interests under this Agreement to any Financing Party (as defined in Exhibit A) for the purpose of securing financing for the Facility. Seller shall provide Buyer with written notice of any such collateral assignment within fifteen (15) Business Days of the effective date thereof, together with a copy of the executed collateral assignment agreement (which may be redacted to remove commercially sensitive terms relating to the financing). Buyer shall, upon Seller\'s request, execute and deliver to Seller and the applicable Financing Party a consent and estoppel agreement in substantially the form attached as Exhibit H, confirming Buyer\'s acknowledgment of such collateral assignment and granting the Financing Party the step-in and cure rights set forth in Section 17.3.

**Section 17.1(b) --- Other Assignments by Seller.** Any assignment of Seller\'s rights or obligations under this Agreement to any Person other than a Financing Party (including, without limitation, assignment in connection with a sale of the Facility or a change of control of Seller, or collateral assignment to any Person not constituting a Financing Party) shall require the prior written consent of Buyer, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. No such assignment shall relieve Seller of its obligations under this Agreement unless and until the assignee has assumed in writing all of Seller\'s obligations hereunder in form and substance reasonably acceptable to Buyer. Buyer may condition its consent on (i) the assignee\'s demonstration of technical capability to operate the Facility, (ii) the assignee\'s creditworthiness being at least equivalent to that of Seller, and (iii) the assignee\'s delivery of replacement credit support, if applicable.

**Section 17.2 --- Assignment by Buyer**

Buyer may not assign its rights or obligations under this Agreement without the prior written consent of Seller, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed; provided, however, that Buyer may assign this Agreement, without Seller\'s consent, to a successor municipal entity or governmental body that (a) expressly assumes all of Buyer\'s obligations under this Agreement in a written instrument delivered to Seller, and (b) has a credit rating at least equivalent to Buyer\'s credit rating as of the date of such assignment or provides credit support reasonably acceptable to Seller. **Section 17.3 --- Lender Step-In Rights**

Buyer agrees to execute and deliver, upon Seller\'s request, a consent and estoppel agreement (a \"Lender Consent\") in substantially the form attached as Exhibit H, granting to the Financing Parties the following rights: (a) the right to receive copies of all notices of default delivered by Buyer to Seller; (b) an additional cure period of one hundred eighty (180) days (following the expiration of any cure period available to Seller under Article 18) within which to cure any default by Seller under this Agreement; (c) the right to assume Seller\'s obligations under this Agreement (directly or through a designee) if the Financing Party elects to exercise step-in rights during the cure period; and (d) the right to receive a replacement power purchase agreement from Buyer on substantially similar terms if this Agreement is terminated due to a Seller default. Buyer agrees not to terminate this Agreement or exercise any other remedy during the Financing Party\'s cure period, so long as the Financing Party has notified Buyer of its intent to cure and is diligently pursuing such cure.

**[ARTICLE 18 --- DEFAULT AND REMEDIES]{.underline}**

**Section 18.1 --- Events of Default by Seller**

Each of the following shall constitute an \"Event of Default\" by Seller:

\(a\) Seller fails to achieve the Commercial Operation Date by the Outside Date (September 1, 2027), subject to extension for Force Majeure events as provided in this Agreement;

\(b\) Any representation or warranty made by Seller in this Agreement is false or misleading in any material respect when made or when deemed repeated;

\(c\) Seller fails to deliver or maintain the Performance Bond as required by Section 13.1, and such failure continues for thirty (30) days after written notice from Buyer;

\(d\) Seller (i) files a petition in bankruptcy or insolvency, or for reorganization or arrangement under any bankruptcy or insolvency laws, (ii) makes an assignment for the benefit of creditors, (iii) consents to the appointment of a receiver or trustee for all or a substantial portion of its assets, or (iv) is the subject of an involuntary petition in bankruptcy that is not dismissed within ninety (90) days;

\(e\) Seller fails to pay any amount due under this Agreement within thirty (30) days after written notice from Buyer that such payment is overdue;

\(f\) Seller materially breaches any other obligation under this Agreement and such breach is not cured within sixty (60) days after written notice from Buyer specifying the breach in reasonable detail; provided that if such breach is of a nature that cannot reasonably be cured within sixty (60) days and Seller has commenced and is diligently pursuing a cure, such cure period shall be extended for an additional sixty (60) days (for a total cure period not to exceed one hundred twenty (120) days).

**Section 18.2 --- Events of Default by Buyer**

Each of the following shall constitute an \"Event of Default\" by Buyer:

\(a\) Buyer fails to pay any amount due under this Agreement within thirty (30) days after written notice from Seller that such payment is overdue;

\(b\) Any representation or warranty made by Buyer in this Agreement is false or misleading in any material respect when made or when deemed repeated;

\(c\) Buyer (i) files a petition in bankruptcy or insolvency, or for reorganization or arrangement under any bankruptcy or insolvency laws, (ii) makes an assignment for the benefit of creditors, or (iii) is the subject of an involuntary proceeding that is not dismissed within ninety (90) days; and

\(d\) Buyer materially breaches any other obligation under this Agreement and such breach is not cured within sixty (60) days after written notice from Seller specifying the breach in reasonable detail.

**Section 18.3 --- Remedies Upon Default**

Upon the occurrence and continuance of an Event of Default (after the expiration of any applicable cure period, including any Financing Party cure period under Section 17.3), the non-defaulting Party may:

\(a\) Terminate this Agreement upon thirty (30) days\' written notice to the defaulting Party, such termination to be effective at the end of such thirty (30) day period (or, if the default is cured during such period, the notice shall be deemed withdrawn);

\(b\) Pursue damages, subject to the limitations set forth in Article 16. In the event of termination by the non-defaulting Party, the non-defaulting Party shall be entitled to recover termination damages calculated as follows: Termination Damages = the present value (discounted at a rate of six percent (6%) per annum) of (i) the expected revenue stream for the remaining Term (calculated as the Contract Quantity multiplied by the applicable Contract Price for each remaining Contract Year) minus (ii) the market value of a replacement contract for equivalent energy and environmental attributes for the remaining Term, based on then-current market conditions as reasonably determined by the non-defaulting Party. If the Termination Damages are a positive number in favor of the non-defaulting Party, the defaulting Party shall pay such amount within sixty (60) days of the non-defaulting Party\'s demand; and

\(c\) Exercise any other rights and remedies available at law or in equity, subject to the limitations set forth in this Agreement.

**Section 18.4 --- Cure Rights of Financing Parties**

In the event of an Event of Default by Seller, Buyer shall provide copies of all notices of default to the Financing Parties identified in writing by Seller (or the applicable Financing Party) simultaneously with delivery of such notices to Seller. The Financing Parties shall be entitled to the cure period and step-in rights set forth in Section 17.3 and as more fully described in the Lender Consent executed pursuant to Exhibit H.

**[ARTICLE 19 --- DISPUTE RESOLUTION]{.underline}**

**Section 19.1 --- Informal Resolution and Mediation**

The Parties shall first attempt to resolve any dispute, controversy, or claim arising under or relating to this Agreement, or the breach, termination, or validity thereof (each, a \"Dispute\"), through good-faith negotiations between senior executives of each Party (each with authority to resolve the Dispute) for a period of thirty (30) days following written notice of the Dispute from one Party to the other (the \"Negotiation Period\"). Such notice shall set forth in reasonable detail the nature of the Dispute and the relief sought. If the Dispute is not resolved during the Negotiation Period, either Party may submit the Dispute to mediation, to be administered by a mutually agreeable mediator in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma. The mediation shall be conducted for a period not to exceed sixty (60) days from the appointment of the mediator. The Parties shall share equally the costs and fees of the mediator. The mediation shall be confidential, and no statements or offers made during mediation shall be admissible as evidence in any subsequent proceeding.

**Section 19.2 --- Litigation**

If the Dispute is not resolved through mediation within the time period specified in Section 19.1, either Party may commence litigation in the District Court of Osage County, State of Oklahoma. Each Party hereby irrevocably consents to the exclusive jurisdiction and venue of the District Court of Osage County, Oklahoma, for the resolution of any Disputes arising under or relating to this Agreement, and waives any objection to such venue, including on grounds of forum non conveniens or lack of personal jurisdiction. Each Party agrees that service of process may be made upon it by certified mail or overnight courier to the address set forth in Section 20.2. Judgment entered by the District Court of Osage County, Oklahoma, may be enforced in any court of competent jurisdiction.

**Section 19.3 --- Provisional Relief**

Nothing in this Article 19 shall prevent either Party from seeking injunctive relief, specific performance, or other provisional or equitable relief from any court of competent jurisdiction at any time, to the extent necessary to prevent irreparable harm or to preserve the status quo pending the resolution of a Dispute.

**Section 19.4 --- Costs**

Except as otherwise ordered by the court, each Party shall bear its own costs and expenses (including attorneys\' fees) in connection with any dispute resolution proceeding under this Article 19. The Parties expressly waive any right to recover attorneys\' fees from the other Party, except to the extent expressly ordered by the court.

**[EXHIBIT C]{.underline}**

**[PROJECT DESCRIPTION]{.underline}**

**Section 1 --- General Description**

**Project Name:** Prairie Crest Wind Project

**Location:** The Facility is located on approximately 14,200 leased acres in Osage County, Oklahoma, approximately twelve (12) miles northwest of the city of Pawhuska. The project site is situated within the boundaries of the Osage Nation, and all necessary approvals from the Osage Minerals Council and the Bureau of Indian Affairs have been obtained or are in the process of being obtained.

**Nameplate Capacity:** 250 MW (nominal).

**Turbine Manufacturer and Model:** Nordex Delta4000, rated at 4.0 MW per turbine.

**Number of Turbines:** Sixty-two (62) Nordex Delta4000 wind turbine generators to be installed on permanent foundations, plus two (2) reserve pads. The reserve pads are prepared foundation locations that may be utilized for replacement or additional turbines at Seller\'s discretion. The total installed turbine capacity is 62 × 4.0 MW = 248 MW, with the 250 MW nameplate achieved through turbine optimization features and the potential future installation of turbines on the two reserve pads.

**SPP Interconnection Queue Position:** GEN-2205.

**Interconnection Voltage:** The Facility collector system operates at 34.5 kV, with voltage step-up to 345 kV at the project substation. The project substation connects to the SPP transmission system via a dedicated 345 kV interconnection line, approximately 4.2 miles in length, terminating at the existing Osage Switchyard.

**Expected Annual Net Generation:** Approximately 876,000 MWh at P50 (corresponding to a net capacity factor of approximately 40.0%).

**Developer/Owner:** Crescent Ridge Wind Partners LLC, a Delaware limited liability company and wholly owned subsidiary of Verdana Renewable Holdings Inc., a Delaware corporation.

**Design Life:** Minimum twenty-five (25) years.

**Section 2 --- Site Description and Layout**

The Prairie Crest Wind Project site is located in the rolling tallgrass prairie of north-central Osage County, Oklahoma. The terrain consists of gently undulating grasslands with elevations ranging from approximately 900 to 1,150 feet above mean sea level. The prevailing wind direction is south-southwesterly, consistent with the Great Plains wind corridor, with average annual hub-height wind speeds of approximately 8.2 meters per second as measured by on-site meteorological towers installed in 2022 and 2023.

The turbine layout has been optimized using industry-standard micrositing software to maximize energy capture while minimizing wake losses and complying with all applicable setback requirements. Turbines are arranged in a generally north-south orientation, with inter-turbine spacing of approximately 4 to 5 rotor diameters in the prevailing wind direction and 8 to 10 rotor diameters in the crosswind direction. All turbine locations comply with a minimum setback of 1,500 feet from existing occupied dwellings and property boundaries.

The project includes approximately 62 miles of internal access roads, a 34.5 kV underground and overhead collector system connecting each turbine to the project substation, a centralized operations and maintenance building, and meteorological towers for ongoing wind resource monitoring.

**Section 3 --- Mechanical Availability Calculation Methodology**

Mechanical Availability for each Contract Year shall be calculated as follows:

Mechanical Availability (%) = (Total Hours -- Planned Maintenance Hours -- Unplanned Outage Hours Attributable to Mechanical Failure) / (Total Hours -- Planned Maintenance Hours) × 100%

Where:

> • \"Total Hours\" means the total number of hours in the applicable Contract Year (8,760 hours, or 8,784 in a leap year);
>
> • \"Planned Maintenance Hours\" means the aggregate hours during which any turbine was offline for planned maintenance activities conducted in accordance with Section 9.2 of the Agreement, weighted by the rated capacity of each affected turbine as a fraction of the total installed capacity;
>
> • \"Unplanned Outage Hours Attributable to Mechanical Failure\" means the aggregate hours during which any turbine was offline due to mechanical, electrical, or equipment failure (including gearbox, generator, blade, yaw system, pitch system, and control system failures), weighted by the rated capacity of each affected turbine as a fraction of the total installed capacity.

The following categories of downtime shall be excluded from both the numerator and denominator of the Mechanical Availability calculation: (a) grid outages, including SPP-directed curtailment and transmission system failures; (b) System Curtailment as defined in Section 6.1(b); (c) Force Majeure events as defined in Section 12.1; (d) Buyer-caused outages or delays; and (e) periods during which wind speeds are below the turbine cut-in speed or above the turbine cut-out speed.

The Guaranteed Mechanical Availability is ninety-five percent (95%) per Contract Year, as set forth in Section 8.7 of the Agreement.

**Section 4 --- Turbine Specifications**

The following are the principal specifications for the Nordex Delta4000 4.0 MW wind turbine generator:

> • **Rated Power Output:** 4,000 kW (4.0 MW)
>
> • **Rotor Diameter:** Approximately 149 meters
>
> • **Hub Height:** Approximately 105 meters (site-specific; final hub height to be determined based on micrositing and geotechnical analysis)
>
> • **Cut-In Wind Speed:** Approximately 3.0 m/s
>
> • **Rated Wind Speed:** Approximately 12.0 m/s
>
> • **Cut-Out Wind Speed:** Approximately 25.0 m/s (with storm ride-through capability)
>
> • **IEC Wind Turbine Class:** IEC Class IIA
>
> • **Drive Train:** Geared (three-stage planetary/helical gearbox)
>
> • **Generator Type:** Doubly-fed induction generator (DFIG)
>
> • **Yaw System:** Active, electric
>
> • **Design Life:** Minimum 20 years (with service life extension potential to 25+ years)
>
> • **Certification:** Type-certified in accordance with IEC 61400 series standards

Detailed turbine specifications, including the manufacturer\'s warranted power curve, are maintained by Seller and shall be made available to Buyer upon reasonable request.

**Section 2 --- Meter Installation and Commissioning**

2.1 Seller shall complete the installation of all metering equipment prior to the commencement of commissioning testing of the Facility. Installation shall be performed by qualified metering technicians in accordance with the manufacturer\'s installation instructions and applicable industry standards.

2.2 Upon completion of installation, all metering equipment shall be subjected to acceptance testing, including: (a) verification of CT and VT ratios and phase relationships; (b) calibration of each meter to within ±0.2% of the reference standard; (c) verification of interval data recording and telemetry functions; (d) end-to-end communication testing with Buyer\'s data systems; and (e) verification of test switch and bypass switch functionality.

2.3 The results of acceptance testing shall be documented in a commissioning report and provided to Buyer within ten (10) Business Days of completion. Buyer shall have the right to witness acceptance testing upon reasonable advance notice to Seller.

**Section 3 --- Calibration Protocols**

3.1 Seller shall cause all revenue meters to be calibrated at least once per calendar year by a qualified, independent testing organization acceptable to both Parties. Calibration shall be performed in accordance with ANSI C12.1 standards and the protocols specified in this Section 3.

3.2 Calibration shall include: (a) comparison of each meter against a portable reference standard of accuracy class 0.05% or better; (b) testing at no less than three load points (light load, mid-load, and full load); (c) verification of the accuracy of all CTs and VTs; and (d) adjustment of any meter found to deviate from the reference standard by more than ±0.2%.

3.3 If any meter is found to be inaccurate by more than ±0.5%, the provisions of Article 7, Section 7.2 of the Agreement shall apply with respect to billing adjustments.

3.4 Calibration reports shall be provided to Buyer within fifteen (15) Business Days of completion of each calibration test.

**Section 4 --- Data Collection and Telemetry**

4.1 The metering system shall record interval data in fifteen (15) minute intervals, synchronized to the SPP market settlement clock.

4.2 Meter data shall be transmitted in real-time to Buyer via a secure electronic interface (encrypted VPN or equivalent) in a format compatible with Buyer\'s energy management system. Seller shall provide Buyer with login credentials and system access sufficient to permit real-time monitoring of meter data.

4.3 In the event of a telemetry failure, Seller shall use commercially reasonable efforts to restore telemetry within twenty-four (24) hours. During any period of telemetry failure, Seller shall manually read and record meter data at intervals of no greater than one (1) hour and shall transmit such data to Buyer within twenty-four (24) hours.

4.4 All meter data shall be stored in a secure, redundant data management system maintained by Seller, with automated daily backups.

**Section 5 --- Meter Testing Procedures**

5.1 **Routine Tests.** In addition to the annual calibration described in Section 3, Seller shall perform visual inspections of all metering equipment on a quarterly basis and shall verify the integrity of all seals, connections, and enclosures.

5.2 **Special Tests.** Either Party may request a special meter test at any time by providing ten (10) Business Days\' written notice to the other Party. Special tests shall be performed by a qualified, independent testing organization acceptable to both Parties. The cost of a special test shall be borne by the requesting Party unless the meter is found to be inaccurate by more than ±0.5%, in which case the cost shall be borne by Seller.

5.3 **Test Results.** The results of all routine inspections and special tests shall be documented and provided to both Parties within fifteen (15) Business Days of completion.

**Section 6 --- Adjustment Procedures for Meter Inaccuracy**

6.1 If any revenue meter is found to be inaccurate by more than ±0.5%, the meter readings shall be adjusted for billing purposes in accordance with Section 7.2 of the Agreement.

6.2 The adjustment shall be calculated by applying the percentage error to the metered energy for the applicable adjustment period. If the meter was over-registering, Buyer shall receive a credit; if the meter was under-registering, Seller shall receive additional payment.

6.3 Adjusted amounts shall be reflected in the next Monthly Invoice following the determination of the adjustment, or, if the adjustment amount exceeds \$100,000, the Party owing the net amount may elect to pay in three (3) equal monthly installments.

**Section 7 --- Check Metering**

7.1 Buyer shall have the right to install, own, operate, and maintain check meters at or near the Delivery Point, at Buyer\'s sole cost and expense. Check meters shall be of a type and accuracy class reasonably acceptable to Seller and shall not interfere with the operation of the revenue meters.

7.2 Check meter data shall be used for verification purposes only and shall not be the basis for billing unless the revenue meters are unavailable or inaccurate, in which case check meter data shall be used as the primary billing data until the revenue meters are repaired or replaced.

7.3 Buyer shall provide Seller with reasonable access to check meter data upon request.

**Section 8 --- Data Retention**

8.1 Seller shall retain all meter data, calibration records, test reports, and related documentation for a minimum period of seven (7) years following the date of generation of such data or records.

8.2 Upon the expiration or termination of this Agreement, Seller shall transfer copies of all meter data and records to Buyer in an electronic format reasonably specified by Buyer.

st.element.rPr.rFonts.set(qn("w:eastAsia"), "Calibri")

doc.add_heading("1. Executive Summary", level=1)
para("**Bottom line.** The executed PPA does **not** conform to the Binding Term Sheet in all material respects, and Checklist Item 12 cannot be answered “consistent.” We identified **26 deviations** plus a set of ancillary drafting inconsistencies. para("**Financial close risk: RED (high).** As executed, the PPA will not support an April 15, 2025 close with Ridgeline. Three issues are, in our view, independently close-blocking:")
bullet("**Tax equity excluded from “Financing Party” (D-1/D-2).** Exhibit A limits “Financing Party” to senior secured lenders and their agents; Exhibit H §8 goes further and expressly states that any assignment to a “tax equity investor, partnership-flip partner, or similar equity investor” requires Buyer consent under §17.1(b). Ridgeline therefore has no consent-free collateral assignment, cure, step-in or replacement-PPA rights. Ms. Kowalski’s summary records Ridgeline’s position that this is non-negotiable (“Ridgeline won’t close”). This is directly contrary to Term Sheet §1 and §15.1 and to Mr. Langdon’s January 17 assurance.")
bullet("**Admitting Ridgeline as a member may itself breach the PPA (D-3).** The partnership-flip requires amending and restating Seller’s LLC Agreement (Checklist Item 2). bullet("**Exhibit B price table does not tie to the 1.5% escalator (D-4).** Exhibit B is built on an approximately **2.0%** escalator (Year 6 $39.27 vs. $39.08 under the formula; Year 20 $51.80 vs. $48.13). At the Contract Quantity the table overstates Years 6–20 revenue by **~$23.18 million nominal (~$9.58 million PV at 6%)**. Section 4.2(a) says prices “shall be as set forth in” Exhibit B while §4.2(b) states the formula and §1.3 makes the body control — an internal conflict that Ridgeline’s model (Item 40) and Elkhorn’s base case cannot underwrite. The table must be corrected by amendment.")
para("Several further deviations will be treated by Ridgeline/Elkhorn as material even if not individually close-blocking: litigation in Osage County District Court instead of confidential AAA arbitration (D-11; Item 43); omission of the Buyer-bears-100% new-transmission-charge carve-out (D-10; Item 22); economic curtailment compensation at 80% rather than 90% (D-5); Delay LDs of $175,000/month capped at $2.5M rather than $125,000/month capped at $1.5M (D-6), combined with an evergreen Outside Date and Event-of-Default/termination-damages exposure that eliminates the Term Sheet’s sole-remedy construct (D-7); a 12-month (not 18-month) force majeure termination right (D-8); Availability LDs at $65,000 (not $50,000) per point and outside the 20% combined LD cap (D-12/D-13); and a performance bond due within 30 days of the Effective Date (i.e., by **March 6, 2025**) with no step-down (D-21/D-22).")
para("**Why this cannot be fixed by pointing to the Term Sheet.** PPA §20.3 supersedes the Term Sheet “to the extent inconsistent,” the PPA recitals say the same, and Term Sheet §18.5 itself provides that the Definitive PPA controls in any conflict (the Term Sheet survives only as an aid to interpreting genuine ambiguity). The Term Sheet is therefore useful for D-4 (where the PPA is internally ambiguous) but not for the clear textual deviations. Each must be remedied by a written amendment signed by both Parties (§20.4), which for Buyer will likely require Board of Trustees action and compliance with public-meeting requirements (§11.2(b), (g)). That process is the critical path to April 15.")
para("**Recommended path.** Open a single “First Amendment to PPA” package with Prescott & Hale immediately (target delivery of draft by March 7, 2025), anchored on (i) the Financing Party / Exhibit H / change-of-control / §11.1(g) fixes and (ii) restoring the Term Sheet terms for each non-agreed deviation. Seller holds real currency for the trade: correcting Exhibit B to the 1.5% formula is worth ~$23.2 million nominal to Buyer, and Seller can offer to document the agreed quarterly generation reports. In parallel, deliver this report (Ridgeline version) to Ridgeline on or before March 14 with the remediation plan, and confirm the performance bond is (or will be) delivered by March 6 to avoid an independent compliance problem. See Section 7.")

doc.add_heading("2. Scope, Documents and Method", level=1)
para("Documents reviewed in full:")
bullet("Binding Term Sheet dated November 8, 2024, Seller/Buyer, 18 sections plus Annex A (Indicative Contract Price Schedule) (the “Term Sheet” or “TS”).")
bullet("Power Purchase Agreement dated as of February 4, 2025, prepared by Prescott & Hale LLP, Articles 1–20 and Exhibits A–H (the “PPA”).")
bullet("Email from Dana Kowalski (Verdana) to Catherine Ainsworth, cc Ryan Matsuda and Marcus Ellington, dated January 22, 2025, “Re: Prairie Crest PPA — Negotiation Summary and Open Items” (the “Negotiation Summary”).")
bullet("Ridgeline Tax Equity Due Diligence Checklist (45 items) and Status Tracker (the “Checklist”).")
para("Method: clause-by-clause comparison of every Term Sheet commercial term against the PPA body and exhibits; each difference classified by negotiation status (using the Negotiation Summary as the only record of agreement), direction of impact on Seller/financing parties, and severity for financial close; and mapped to the relevant Checklist item. Figures were recomputed independently (price tables, LD and curtailment exposure).")
para("Classification key:", bold=True, space_after=2)
table(["Status code", "Meaning"], [
 ("AGREED", "Departure Seller agreed to in negotiations (per Negotiation Summary §1). Not documented by Term Sheet amendment or side letter."),
 ("OPEN-IN PPA", "Item listed as “still being discussed” in Negotiation Summary §4 that nonetheless appears in executed PPA; agreement trail must be confirmed."),
 ("NOT AGREED", "Contrary to a term Seller expressly said must track the Term Sheet (Negotiation Summary §2–§3), or otherwise not agreed."),
 ("NEW TERM", "PPA provision with no Term Sheet counterpart that changes the commercial risk allocation."),
 ("DRAFTING", "Internal inconsistency, arithmetic or factual error."),
], widths=(1.3, 5.4), size=8.5)
para("Severity: **Critical** = close-blocking for Ridgeline absent cure; **High** = material to Ridgeline/Elkhorn underwriting and should be fixed pre-close; **Medium** = should be fixed or expressly disclosed/accepted; **Low** = disclosure or clean-up.", size=9.5)
EOF

I wrote the deviation report. It finds that the executed PPA departs from the binding term sheet in 26 places, and that financial close is at high risk (RED). Three problems would each block close on their own:
- **Tax equity excluded:** the PPA's "Financing Party" definition leaves out tax equity investors, and Exhibit H §8 says outright that they need Buyer consent.
- **Change of control and ownership:** admitting Ridgeline as a member would need Buyer consent under the change-of-control clause, and would make Seller's sole-ownership representation untrue when it is repeated at COD.
- **Price table:** the Exhibit B table is built on roughly a 2% escalator, not 1.5%, overstating revenue by about $23.2M.

Only two deviations were actually agreed: the 75% performance guarantee threshold and the 50% shortfall LD rate. Two more (Seller keeping excess RECs, and early COD from March 1, 2026) were still under discussion in the January email but appear in the signed PPA. The report recommends a single First Amendment to fix the rest, and maps each deviation to the tax equity checklist items with a remediation timeline back from the April 15, 2025 close.
